facts.text: Device is the Python object representing one Multi-Tube-OD-Reader instrument
The Device constructor keeps a list of Port objects for physical positions 1 through 16
Device.discovery enumerates connected U3 devices with u3.openAllU3() and creates one Device per serial number
Device.connect opens u3.U3 by serial number and returns the LabJack U3 interface
Device.rename writes the new name with U3.setName and updates the Device name
Device.blink toggles the built-in LED and DAC0 in 25 passes with 0.15 s between passes
The clone opens and closes the LabJack connection at each timepoint so parallel experiments can share the hardware
After discovery the clone closes all U3 connections with Close() so other experiments can use the hardware
measure_voltage maps port numbers to AIN positions (port number minus one) and sets the FIO/EIO analog masks for the requested ports
DAC0 powers the LED/sensor relay and DAC1 the linear regulator to the sensors; the configured voltages are 5 V and 2.6 V
measure_voltage sets the DAC voltages before sampling and returns both DACs to 0 after sampling
measure_voltage averages n_reps calibrated analog voltage samples and returns one mean per requested port
measure_temp reads the U3 internal temperature in Kelvin and converts it to Celsius
The README states that the repository controls a 16-tube, in-line optical density monitoring device
The README says raw measurements are voltages and that log10(voltage) is fitted to known optical densities offline
The README requires a U3-compatible LabJack driver: UD on Windows, Exodriver on Linux/macOS
The pinned requirements file lists LabJackPython 2.1.0
